report.verdict: A flat nine months that hides a Q3 downturn: 9M-26 BSI (GGR) +0.5% to DKK 3,841m (~$568m) and net profit +1.5% to DKK 1,547m (~$229m) were carried entirely by H1; derived Q3 BSI fell 1.4% to DKK 1,255m (~$186m) and net profit fell 4.2% to DKK 503m (~$74m) as the lottery jackpot cycle turned (Danske Lotteri Spil -5.9%) and only cost cuts and a +7.5% licensed-games segment held EBIT margin flat at 52.7%. FY26 guidance (BSI DKK 5,200–5,300m / net profit DKK 1,950–2,050m) is unchanged and, with an October Eurojackpot max-pool run, remains achievable in the upper half — but the equity story is a monopoly lottery cash-cow with a shrinking retail footprint and a sub-scale, duty-heavy online business that is not out-growing its market.
summary: **Headline in line with the run-rate, no consensus to beat.** Danske Spil A/S (unlisted, Danish state-controlled; FY ends 31 Dec; IFRS recognition/measurement; unaudited quarterly) reported 9M-26 gross gaming revenue (BSI) of DKK 3,841m (~$568m), +0.5% (+DKK 21m) YoY, EBIT of DKK 2,004m (~$296m), +2.2%, and net profit of DKK 1,547m (~$229m), +1.5% (+DKK 23m). All figures are reported IFRS; the company publishes no adjusted metrics.

**Q3 standalone turned negative.** Derived Q3-26 (9M less H1): BSI DKK 1,255m (~$186m), -1.4% YoY and -9.2% QoQ; EBIT DKK 662m (~$98m), -1.3%; net profit DKK 503m (~$74m), -4.2% YoY. The 2026 quarterly BSI path is now Q1 -5.6%, Q2 +8.7% (record Eurojackpot May draw + World Cup), Q3 -1.4% — i.e. the year is being made or lost by the jackpot calendar.

**Mix: licensed games up, lottery down — the division that drove the quarter was Danske Lotteri Spil (negatively).** 9M BSI: Danske Lotteri Spil DKK 2,193m (~$324m), -2.1% (Q3 -5.9%); Danske Licens Spil DKK 1,238m (~$183m), +6.6% (Q3 +7.5%); Klasselotteriet DKK 205m (~$30m), -2.4%; Elite Gaming DKK 204m (~$30m), -2.9%. Management cites fewer Eurojackpot high pools, smaller Lotto pools and lower in-store Quick scratchcard sales, only partly offset by Vikinglotto; licensed growth came from online casino and the new poker platform.

**Profit growth is a cost story, not a revenue story.** Gross profit from games fell 0.3% to DKK 2,881m (~$426m) (margin 75.0%, -67bps) as gaming duties rose DKK 17m to DKK 474m (~$70m) and other gaming-related (platform/content) costs rose DKK 34m (+16.6%). Below that, 'other costs incl. D&A' fell DKK 55m (-5.7%) to DKK 902m (~$133m): other external costs -DKK 30m (lower marketing), staff -DKK 13m, D&A -DKK 13m. Every krone of the DKK 44m EBIT improvement came from opex.

**Margins: group EBIT margin 52.2% (+87bps 9M); Q3 flat at 52.7%.** Danske Lotteri Spil EBIT margin 73.7% (+134bps), Danske Licens Spil 18.6% (+264bps), Klasselotteriet 71.2% (+598bps). Derived EBITDA (EBIT + D&A) DKK 2,122m (~$314m), +1.5%, margin 55.2% (+51bps). Net margin 40.3% (+38bps); effective tax rate 22.2%.

**Guidance unchanged, but now explicitly carved around the Elite Gaming disposal.** FY26 BSI DKK 5,200–5,300m (~$769–784m) and net profit DKK 1,950–2,050m (~$288–303m), 'excluding the conditional sale of Elite Gaming'. Implied Q4-26: BSI DKK 1,359–1,459m vs Q4-25 DKK 1,338m (+1.6% to +9.0%); net profit DKK 403–503m vs Q4-25 DKK 484m (-16.7% to +3.9%). The profit range midpoint implies a Q4 decline, which looks conservative given October's Eurojackpot max pool.

**Portfolio simplification: Elite Gaming (land-based slots) being sold.** Announced 17 Sep 2026 to 87KDSL A/S (owner of Dan-Automater Struer; Erhvervsinvest-backed), approved at an EGM on 16 Sep, conditional on Danish Competition and Consumer Authority clearance; price undisclosed. Elite Gaming is 5.3% of 9M BSI but only 0.4% of EBIT (DKK 9m, ~$1m) with segment assets of DKK 72m (~$11m); effect will be booked on completion.

**Capital position is fortress-like and debt-free.** 30 Sep: cash DKK 1,399m (~$207m) + securities DKK 832m (~$123m) = DKK 2,231m (~$330m), +2.5% YoY; equity DKK 1,851m (~$274m), equity ratio 58.8%; no borrowings disclosed (long-term liabilities DKK 97m). 9M operating cash flow DKK 1,860m (~$275m), -3.4%, 93% of EBIT (vs 98%); capex (additions) DKK 127m (~$19m), -8.6%; derived FCF DKK 1,733m (~$256m).

**Distributions: DKK 1,094m (~$162m) paid to owners in 9M-26** (vs DKK 1,164m), per the equity statement — Danske Spil distributes essentially all profit via the state 'udlodningsmidler' (FY25: DKK 1.8bn to good causes; total societal contribution incl. duties and corporate tax DKK 3,148m (~$466m)). No buybacks (state-owned, DKK 1m share capital; EPS not meaningful).

**Financial items are noise but swung the quarter.** 9M financial items -DKK 16m (vs -DKK 5m); Q3 alone -DKK 17m after +DKK 26m in Q2 (unrealised securities gains) and -DKK 25m in Q1 — DKK 43m QoQ swing explains most of the Q3 PBT drop (-15.9% QoQ) beyond operations.

**Retail network is contracting fast.** Dealers 3,464 at 30 Sep vs 3,759 a year ago (-295, -7.8%) and 3,622 at 30 Jun (-158 in one quarter). Dealer commission fell DKK 21m (-7.8%) to 6.4% of BSI; c.70% of group sales were online in FY25. Good for margin, bad for Quick scratchcards and impulse lottery sales.

**Headcount up, staff cost down, capitalisation up — watch.** Average FTEs 480 (+1.7%) while staff costs fell 4.5%; additions to the reserve for development projects (capitalised development) rose to DKK 122m (~$18m) from DKK 99m. Not alarming at this scale, but P&L support from capitalisation should be monitored.

**No formal cost-transformation programme exists.** Savings are ad hoc (marketing, D&A roll-off, procurement) with no quantified multi-year target disclosed — n/a. The 9M opex reduction of DKK 55m is the only hard number.

**Market context (Danish Gambling Authority, secondary): Q3 was a volatile betting quarter and a strong casino quarter.** July total market +17.2% (online casino +22%, betting +21.3%, World Cup final); August -7.1% to DKK 678m (betting -42.7% to DKK 132m; online casino +12.5% to DKK 415m); September +22.1% to DKK 685m (betting +64.6%; online casino DKK 400m, +17.9%, 58% of market GGR). Danske Licens Spil's +7.5% total Q3 growth implies it is trailing market online-casino growth of mid/high-teens — share loss risk, with Stake's entry flagged in the FY25 report.

**Regulation: 'Spilpakke 1' (broad political agreement, 24 Oct 2025)** — advertising restrictions (ban on celebrities/experts in gambling ads, minimum 25-year age for ad participants, TV 'whistle-to-whistle' ban in the agreement), tougher action against unlicensed operators, dealer approval scheme. The implementing bill (L 127) lapsed; new legislation was proposed in October 2026 for 2027. Marketing curbs structurally favour the highest-awareness incumbent — Danske Spil welcomed the deal — but also cap its own Oddset marketing.

**Responsible-gambling positioning is explicitly a revenue headwind.** Management again states its higher standards (AI 'spilscanner', deposit limits, under-25 online spend held below DKK 130/month in FY25) weigh on BSI versus the rest of the market. This is the quid pro quo for the lottery monopoly and should be read as a permanent growth drag on Danske Licens Spil.

**Lottery monopoly remains the engine.** Danske Lotteri Spil delivered 81% of 9M segment EBIT (DKK 1,617m of DKK 2,002m ex-parent); Klasselotteriet another 7%. Licensed games (DLiS) are 32% of BSI but only 11% of segment EBIT after the 28% GGR duty and rising platform costs.

**Management/board: no changes.** CEO Nikolas Lyhne-Knudsen and CFO Søren Skovdal Rasmussen signed the report in Copenhagen on 12 Nov 2026; chair Lars Krarup, deputy Charlotte Bach Thomassen; two new employee-elected directors since Q3-25. Subsequent events: none disclosed.

**Thesis read-through.** Earnings are defensible (52% EBIT margin, zero debt, ~90%+ cash conversion) but structurally ex-growth: FY26 guidance midpoints (BSI DKK 5,250m, net profit DKK 2,000m) are +1.8%/-0.4% on FY25. The variables that matter are the Eurojackpot/Lotto pool cycle (Q4 starts with a 750m max pool in October), the pace of online-casino share loss, and the 2027 advertising regime — not anything management controls quarter to quarter.

segments.name: Danske Lotteri Spil (lottery monopoly: Lotto, Eurojackpot, Vikinglotto, Keno, Quick, Alt eller Intet, Spil Sammen, Plus)
segments.headline: The whole 9M shortfall landed in Q3: BSI -5.9% to DKK 717m on a soft jackpot cycle and retail scratchcard erosion, yet EBIT margin rose 164bps to 74.5% on marketing and commission savings.
narrative: They retained their exclusive lottery licence position (Danske Lotteri Spil holds the statutory monopoly for number games and scratchcards in Denmark) and, on Danish Gambling Authority figures for 2025 cited in secondary coverage, the lottery category was just under DKK 3.5bn of GGR, of which DLS alone generated DKK 3,011m (~$445m) — roughly 85% of the category, and over 90% together with Klasselotteriet [estimate from secondary data]. Nine-month BSI came in at DKK 2,193m (~$324m), down 2.1% or DKK 46m, after a first half that was exactly flat (DKK 1,476m vs 1,477m). The derived third quarter was therefore the problem: DKK 717m (~$106m), -5.9% year on year and -12.2% sequentially from a DKK 817m Q2 that had been inflated by a record Eurojackpot draw in May (358,000 tickets for a single DKK 750m draw) and the Easter Lotto. Management attributed the decline to fewer high pools on Eurojackpot, smaller Lotto pools and a fall in Quick scratchcard sales in stores, only partially offset by growth in Vikinglotto. The comparison was also demanding: Q3-25 had grown 5.2% on Eurojackpot and Quick strength.

Profit held up far better than revenue. Segment EBIT was DKK 1,617m (~$239m) for the nine months, -0.2% (DKK -4m) on DKK -46m of BSI, lifting margin 134bps to 73.7%; the derived Q3 EBIT was DKK 534m (~$79m), -3.8%, with margin up 164bps to 74.5% (Q2-26: 75.4%). The levers are visible at group level: dealer commission fell DKK 21m (-7.8%) to 6.4% of BSI as sales migrate online (c.70% of group sales were digital in FY25), marketing was cut within other external costs (-DKK 30m), and D&A declined DKK 13m. Segment capex additions fell to DKK 51m from DKK 73m. DLS remains the group's economic core — 81% of nine-month segment EBIT — and it is this profit that flows to the state 'udlodningsmidler' (DKK 1.8bn to sport, culture and good causes in FY25), which is why the state cares more about its stability than its growth.

The retail footprint is shrinking at a pace that deserves attention: 3,464 dealers at 30 September versus 3,759 a year earlier (-295, -7.8%) and 3,622 at 30 June — 158 outlets lost in a single quarter. The in-store Quick decline cited by management is the first-order consequence; the second-order risk is losing impulse and jackpot-chasing purchases from the roughly 30% of customers who still buy in kiosks and supermarkets. Management frames the online shift as responsibility-led (the digital channel allows limits, AI monitoring and the Spil med omtanke tools) and margin-accretive, and the numbers support the margin point, but a 7.8% annual contraction in physical distribution is not costless for a product whose weekly habit is anchored in retail.

Looking into Q4, the set-up is more favourable than Q3. The Eurojackpot pool rolled from DKK 508m on 25 September through DKK 578m and DKK 673m to the DKK 750m (~$111m) cap by 6 October, and remained at the cap for at least three further draws until it was won on 13 October — the first max-pool run since May and a direct tailwind for October BSI. Against that, Q4-25 is a hard comparison: it included a DKK 149m Danish Eurojackpot winner on 2 December (signalling a high-pool run) and record Christmas sales for Det Store Jule Lotto and Quick's Christmas products. On our arithmetic the FY25 Q4 DLS BSI was DKK 772m (FY25 DKK 3,011m less 9M DKK 2,239m); we pencil in roughly flat to +3% for Q4-26 (DKK 770–795m, estimate), i.e. FY26 DLS BSI of about DKK 2,960–2,990m, -1% to -2%. The company does not guide at segment level. Regulatory marketing curbs under Spilpakke 1 (no celebrities or experts in gambling advertising, 25-year minimum age for ad participants) apply to lottery advertising too, but with brand awareness at saturation this is a minor constraint for DLS compared with its impact on challengers in licensed games.

segments.name: Danske Licens Spil (licensed games: Oddset/eOddset/Tips sportsbook, Casino, Live Casino, Tivoli Casino, Poker, Bingo)
segments.headline: Growth segment of the group (+6.6% 9M / +7.5% Q3) with EBIT +24% and margin +264bps — but with no product split disclosed and the Danish online-casino market growing mid/high-teens, the evidence points to share loss.
narrative: They grew nine-month BSI 6.6% (+DKK 77m) to DKK 1,238m (~$183m), with the derived third quarter at DKK 403m (~$60m), +7.5% year on year and -5.2% sequentially from a World Cup-boosted Q2 of DKK 425m. The quarterly trajectory for 2026 reads Q1 +3.5%, Q2 +9.0%, Q3 +7.5%. Management attributed the increase to continued progress in online casino and growth from the new poker platform launched in the first half; sports betting was not called out as a growth driver in the nine-month commentary, although the H1 report had noted a strong World Cup for Oddset. Segment EBIT rose 24.3% to DKK 230m (~$34m) with margin up 264bps to 18.6%; Q3 EBIT was DKK 73m (~$11m), +10.6%, margin 18.1% (+51bps year on year, -47bps versus Q2). For reference, FY25 segment BSI was DKK 1,584m (~$234m) with net profit of DKK 171m, both down on 2024, so 2026 is a clear recovery year for the division. Danske Spil does not disclose handle, net or structural sports margin, promotional spend as a percentage of handle, monthly actives or ARPU for this segment — all n/a — which makes it impossible to separate volume, price and luck.

The market backdrop (Danish Gambling Authority monthly data via secondary coverage) was unusually volatile in betting and consistently strong in casino. July total market GGR rose 17.2% (online casino +22%, betting +21.3% on the World Cup final); August fell 7.1% to DKK 678m as betting collapsed 42.7% to DKK 132m while online casino rose 12.5% to DKK 415m; September rebounded 22.1% to DKK 685m on betting +64.6% and online casino of DKK 400m, +17.9%, which was 58% of the month's market GGR. In 2025 the Danish online-casino vertical was DKK 4.31bn, +12.1%, or 38% of a c.DKK 11.5bn market. Set against that, DLiS's +7.5% in Q3 — a blend of casino, poker, bingo and betting — is unlikely to have matched the casino market's mid/high-teens growth even if betting was a drag; we read this as continued share loss in casino to international operators (the FY25 report flagged Stake's market entry and 'hard competition'). Danske Spil does not publish its market share and we do not have a verified betting-market denominator, so no share figure is given here.

The economics of the segment are structurally thin. The 28% Danish duty on online casino and betting GGR shows up in the group gaming-duty line rising DKK 17m to DKK 474m, which management explicitly tied to higher DLiS BSI; other gaming-related costs (sportsbook, casino, bingo and poker platform and content fees — the group runs OpenBet for sportsbook and EveryMatrix for casino/bingo) rose DKK 34m or 16.6%, so each incremental krone of licensed BSI carries a materially lower gross margin than lottery, which is why the group's gross-profit margin dropped 185bps to 74.5% in Q3 despite the headline mix shift being only two percentage points. The incremental EBIT margin on the DKK 77m BSI increase was nevertheless 58%, achieved by cutting marketing — a strategy that is self-limiting in a market where competitors spend aggressively and that the forthcoming advertising rules will partly impose on everyone anyway.

Policy is the swing factor for the next two years. Spilpakke 1 (24 October 2025) proposed banning celebrities and experts from gambling advertising, a 25-year minimum age for anyone appearing in ads, a whistle-to-whistle TV ban, a dealer-approval scheme and stronger enforcement against unlicensed operators; the implementing bill lapsed and a new proposal was tabled in October 2026 for 2027. For a brand with Danske Spil's unaided awareness the net relative effect is positive, but Oddset loses its sports-ambassador playbook too. Management continues to stress that its responsibility standards (deposit limits, the AI 'spilscanner', under-25 online spend held below DKK 130 a month in FY25) cost it BSI relative to peers — a permanent structural growth discount for this segment. For Q4 we estimate BSI of DKK 445–455m, +5% to +8% on a derived Q4-25 base of DKK 423m (FY25 DKK 1,584m less 9M DKK 1,161m), with no major football tournament and the usual November/December casino seasonality; EBIT margin around 17–18% (estimate).

segments.name: Det Danske Klasselotteri (Klasselotteriet, monthly class lottery since 1753)
segments.headline: Small, high-margin and lapping a product-change boost: BSI -2.4% on fewer players and a higher payout ratio, but EBIT +6.6% with margin up ~600bps to 71.2%.
narrative: They generated nine-month BSI of DKK 205m (~$30m), down 2.4% or DKK 5m, with the derived Q3 at DKK 67m (~$10m), -2.9% year on year and -4.3% versus Q2. Management describes a 'minor decline' linked to the number of players, and in the Q1 report also to a higher payout ratio. The comparison is the key context: 9M-25 BSI had jumped 14% (DKK 210m vs 184m) on the '15 er magisk' product change implemented in Q4-24, so the business is now simply lapping a step-up rather than deteriorating.

Profitability improved despite the top line. Segment EBIT rose 6.6% to DKK 146m (~$22m), with margin up 598bps to 71.2%; the derived Q3 EBIT was DKK 48m (~$7m), +4.3%, at a 71.6% margin (Q3-25: 66.7%; Q2-26: 71.4%). The product has essentially no variable platform cost and limited marketing, so the margin expansion is mostly operating leverage on a stable cost base plus lower amortisation. Capex is negligible (DKK 2m).

The product mechanics — a draw on the 15th of each month with a DKK 46m prize pool and up to 15 million-krone prizes, sold as whole, half, quarter and eighth tickets, largely on subscription — give it annuity-like revenue and a loyal, older customer base; the risk is demographic attrition, which the player-count comment hints at. The segment's balance sheet (segment assets DKK 392m, +4%) is heavy relative to its revenue, reflecting cash and prize provisions rather than operating assets.

For the full year we expect BSI of roughly DKK 270–275m (estimate; FY25 not separately verified from primary sources) and EBIT around DKK 190–195m. Nothing in this segment moves the group needle, but at a 71% margin it contributes 7% of segment EBIT on 5% of BSI and is a steady contributor to the state distributions.

segments.name: Elite Gaming (land-based gaming machines) — held for sale
segments.headline: Non-core and on its way out: BSI -2.9% to DKK 204m, EBIT DKK 9m (4.4% margin); conditional sale to 87KDSL announced 17 Sep 2026, price undisclosed, guidance excludes the effect.
narrative: They reported nine-month BSI of DKK 204m (~$30m), down 2.9% or DKK 6m, with the derived Q3 flat year on year at DKK 67m (~$10m) and -4.3% versus Q2. Segment EBIT edged up to DKK 9m (~$1m) from DKK 8m, a 4.4% margin — the business is 5.3% of group BSI but 0.4% of EBIT, which is the entire rationale for the disposal. Elite Gaming installs and operates land-based gaming machines in Danish arcades and restaurants, has removed more than a quarter of its machines in recent years as part of a shift to server-based digital terminals (company description), and has a workforce in the 20–50 range (secondary registry data).

On 17 September 2026 Danske Spil announced an agreement to sell the subsidiary to 87KDSL A/S, which already owns Dan-Automater Struer A/S (sister company Compugame-DAE manufactures machines) and is ultimately backed by the private-equity fund Erhvervsinvest (secondary). The transaction was approved at an extraordinary general meeting of Danske Spil on 16 September and is conditional on clearance from the Danish Competition and Consumer Authority (Konkurrence- og Forbrugerstyrelsen); the parties agreed not to disclose the price. The CEO framed it as a strategic prioritisation: Elite Gaming has 'limited strategic coherence' with the rest of the group and does not fit future priorities. The buyer's stated aim is to secure profitable slot-machine earnings through consolidation.

Accounting-wise, the Q3 report states the financial effect will be recognised and the presentation adjusted when the deal completes; no held-for-sale reclassification or gain/loss estimate is given, and the segment still carries DKK 72m (~$11m) of assets (down from DKK 94m). Given undisclosed consideration against a small, declining asset base, we would not expect a material gain, but a modest one is plausible if the price reflects the buyer's synergy case; any such item would sit outside the unchanged guidance, which is explicitly 'without recognition of the conditional sale'.

Deconsolidation would strip roughly DKK 270m of annualised BSI (c.5% of group) and about DKK 12m of EBIT, modestly lifting group EBIT margin and gross-profit margin (machine duty and site commissions are high relative to lottery) and removing the group's only exposure to the land-based slot regulatory regime, including the dealer-approval and arcade-definition provisions in Spilpakke 1. For modelling we keep Elite Gaming consolidated through year-end given the pending competition review; closing in Q4 is possible but not assumed.

highlights.text: Licensed games are compounding: Danske Licens Spil BSI +6.6% (9M) / +7.5% (Q3) to DKK 1,238m (~$183m) with EBIT +24.3% to DKK 230m (~$34m) and margin +264bps to 18.6%, driven by online casino and the new poker platform — the segment is already ahead of its FY25 net-profit run-rate.
Cost discipline converted flat revenue into profit growth: 'other costs incl. D&A' -DKK 55m (-5.7%) to DKK 902m (~$133m); group EBIT margin +87bps to 52.2%; derived EBITDA margin 55.2% (+51bps).
Lottery margin resilience: Danske Lotteri Spil EBIT fell only DKK 4m (-0.2%) on a DKK 46m BSI decline, margin +134bps to 73.7% (Q3 74.5%), as online migration cut dealer commission DKK 21m (-7.8%).

Fortress balance sheet: cash + securities DKK 2,231m (~$330m), equity ratio 58.8%, no borrowings disclosed; 9M CFO DKK 1,860m (~$275m) funded DKK 1,094m (~$162m) of distributions and DKK 127m (~$19m) of capex with room to spare.
Portfolio simplification: conditional sale of Elite Gaming removes 5% of BSI that earns a 4% margin, exits the land-based slot regime and sharpens the group into lottery plus digital licensed games.

Q4 lottery tailwind already in hand: Eurojackpot rolled to the DKK 750m (~$111m) cap by 6 October and stayed there until won on 13 October — the first max-pool run since May — ahead of the Christmas Lotto/Quick season.
Klasselotteriet EBIT +6.6% to DKK 146m (~$22m) at a 71.2% margin (+598bps) despite BSI -2.4%, showing the operating leverage of the subscription lottery base.

lowlights.text: Q3 momentum reversed: derived Q3 BSI -1.4% to DKK 1,255m (~$186m), EBIT -1.3%, net profit -4.2% to DKK 503m (~$74m), after H1 had printed +1.5% / +4.6%; the 9M growth is entirely a Q2 jackpot/World Cup artefact.

Lottery top line is in the hands of the pool cycle: Danske Lotteri Spil Q3 BSI -5.9% to DKK 717m (~$106m) on fewer Eurojackpot high pools, smaller Lotto pools and falling in-store Quick sales; FY26 DLS BSI is tracking -1% to -2%.
Retail distribution is eroding fast: dealers 3,464, -295 (-7.8%) YoY and -158 in Q3 alone; the Quick scratchcard decline is the first visible casualty.

Likely share loss in online casino: DLiS +7.5% total growth in Q3 against a Danish online-casino market growing 12.5–22% per month (DGA, secondary) and new entrants (Stake); no handle, margin, actives or ARPU disclosure to diagnose it.

Gross-margin dilution is structural: gaming duties +3.7% to 12.3% of BSI and other gaming-related (platform/content) costs +16.6% to 6.2% of BSI as the mix shifts to 28%-duty licensed games; gross profit from games margin -67bps (9M) / -185bps (Q3).

Financial items swung DKK 43m QoQ (Q3 -DKK 17m vs Q2 +DKK 26m) on securities mark-to-market, and 9M financial items are DKK 11m worse YoY — non-operating noise that will keep moving quarterly net profit.

Thin disclosure and no cost programme: no product split of licensed BSI, no marketing figure, no customer KPIs, no quantified savings target; staff costs -4.5% while FTEs +1.7% and capitalised development additions rose to DKK 122m (~$18m) from DKK 99m.

forecast.intro: Guidance is unchanged for the third time this year: FY26 BSI of DKK 5,200–5,300m (~$769–784m) and net profit of DKK 1,950–2,050m (~$288–303m), as first set with the FY25 annual report on 13 March 2026 — the only edit is the explicit statement that it excludes the conditional Elite Gaming sale. No division drove a change because there was none; what moved inside the year is mix — Danske Licens Spil is running ahead (BSI +6.6%, EBIT +24%) while Danske Lotteri Spil is running behind (BSI -2.1%, Q3 -5.9%) on the jackpot cycle, and opex (-DKK 55m) is bridging the gap. Mechanically, 9M actuals leave an implied Q4 of BSI DKK 1,359–1,459m versus DKK 1,338m in Q4-25 (+1.6% to +9.0%) and net profit DKK 403–503m versus DKK 484m (-16.7% to +3.9%); the profit range midpoint therefore embeds a Q4 decline, which looks conservative after October's Eurojackpot max-pool run.

forecast.view: **Revenue:** we model Q4-26 BSI of DKK 1,410–1,450m (~$209–214m), +5% to +8% YoY (estimate): Danske Lotteri Spil roughly flat to +3% at DKK 770–795m on the October Eurojackpot max pool (DKK 750m cap reached 6 Oct, won 13 Oct) and Christmas products against a tough Q4-25 comp; Danske Licens Spil +5–8% to DKK 445–455m on casino/poker with no tournament tailwind; Klasselotteriet and Elite Gaming c.DKK 70m each (Elite Gaming assumed still consolidated). That lands FY26 BSI at DKK 5,250–5,290m, +1.8% to +2.6% on FY25's DKK 5,158m. **Margin:** group EBIT margin should hold around 52% for the year (Q4 seasonally similar to Q3; marketing is being held down and D&A keeps rolling off), with gross-profit margin drifting lower as licensed mix rises — we see FY26 EBIT of roughly DKK 2,700–2,740m (estimate). Net profit of DKK 2,000–2,040m assumes financial items near zero in Q4 and a 22% tax rate; a repeat of Q3's securities loss would shave c.DKK 15–20m. **Leverage:** none — net cash of c.DKK 2.2bn at 30 September will be partly distributed; the pattern (DKK 1,094m paid in Q2, nothing in Q3) suggests the balance of the FY25 profit and an on-account FY26 distribution fall in Q4/Q1, so expect year-end cash plus securities around DKK 1.5–2.0bn with no debt. **Swing factors:** (1) jackpot rollovers in Lotto/Eurojackpot through December — each max-pool week is worth tens of millions of BSI; (2) sports results in a tournament-free Q4 (the Danish betting market swung -43% to +65% month-to-month in Q3); (3) timing of the Elite Gaming completion and any disposal gain/loss, which sits outside guidance; (4) securities mark-to-market; (5) the FY27 guidance and 2027 advertising legislation at the March 2027 annual report, where we would expect another 'stable' range (BSI c.DKK 5.0–5.2bn ex-Elite Gaming, net profit c.DKK 1.95–2.05bn) rather than growth.
watch: Q4 lottery pool cycle: number of Eurojackpot draws at or near the DKK 750m cap and Lotto/Vikinglotto rollovers through December versus the Q4-25 comp (DKK 149m Danish Eurojackpot win on 2 Dec 2025; record Christmas Lotto/Quick).
Danish Gambling Authority monthly data (Oct–Dec 2026): whether online-casino market growth stays in the mid/high-teens while DLiS grows high single digits — the share-loss question.
Elite Gaming completion: Competition and Consumer Authority clearance, the deconsolidation date, and any gain/loss booked outside guidance.
Retail dealer count at year-end (3,464 at 30 Sep, -7.8% YoY) and the trajectory of in-store Quick scratchcard sales.
FY26 distribution to udlodningsmidler and FY27 guidance in the March 2027 annual report, including how the 2027 advertising legislation (successor to Spilpakke 1 / lapsed bill L 127) is reflected.
Cost quality: staff costs vs FTE growth, capitalised development additions (DKK 122m 9M-26 vs DKK 99m), and whether marketing is held down into a competitive Q4.
Financial items: securities portfolio (DKK 832m) mark-to-market after a DKK 43m QoQ swing in Q3.
